note: THE WORKTREE FRESHNESS GUARD IS DEAD ON THE MAC, AND THE MAC IS THE ONLY BOX THAT RUNS IT. Running bash -n on scripts/test-worktree-freshness.sh fails under macOS system bash 3.2 (/bin/bash, 3.2.57) with a syntax error near an unexpected open-paren token at line 181. Line 181 is the END block of the awk program that prints the and-N-more remainder, and the U+2026 ellipsis literal inside that single-quoted awk body defeats 3.2 lexing. shellcheck reports the file CLEAN, no output and exit 0, so the defect is invisible both to the linter and to lefford, which has bash 5. Observed live: make worktree-take NAME=the-penstock printed the syntax error immediately after reporting the recycled worktree warm, i.e. the inherited target/ was never checked for stale-name contamination at all. The commit-gate comments record that this call was deliberately moved OUT of the commit gate and INTO worktree-take.sh because the rename is where the condition is created, so on darwin that placement currently protects nothing. Fix is one ASCII substitution in the awk printf. Second lesson: a board note must contain no backticks and no double quotes, make re-expands the recipe so backticks become command substitution and double quotes get word-split into bogus key=value args.
